interpretation.plain_speak: One refresh does not save the memory forever, but it reliably buys time. Every targeted arm lasted longer, often by roughly 7 to 17 writes, while the sham action generally made things slightly worse. The warning-to-action link is therefore real; the one-action budget was simply too small for permanent survival.
interpretation.north_star_question: A bounded corrective response can measurably postpone failure. The next minimal escalation is two warning-triggered targeted actions, not an unbounded maintenance loop.
interpretation.next_stage: test at most two targeted refreshes per arm, each triggered by a fresh warning after the previous action, against a same-budget sham control
